issues.description: fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of being absent from the type
issues.detail: The backward format keeps a writer method on its public surface that always throws. That complects 'this is a reader-only codec' with 'this is a writer' at the type level. A cleaner decomposition: the backwards type implements only the reader path; writing lives in the test-only RW subclass. Throwing at runtime is the easy fix, not the simple one.

issues.description: Writer capability re-attached via test-only RW subclasses recreates the concern the move was meant to separate
issues.detail: Moving formats to backward-codecs is supposed to mean 'read-only.' But Lucene99RWScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat and the RW HNSW variants reintroduce writing by subclassing and overriding fieldsWriter. The read/write identity is now smeared across a base class and a test subclass that share package-private state. A data-described 'version + capability' would let one reader and one (test-only) writer compose without inheritance games.

issues.description: Visibility downgrade of fields from protected to package-private silently widens the test-subclass contract
issues.detail: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues fields went from protected to package-private. That hides them from external subclasses but keeps them mutable shared state for everything in this package, including the test RW classes. The intent ('no one outside extends this anymore') is good; the mechanism complects 'frozen for outside' with 'still a shared mutable surface inside.' Consider final + accessors, or moving the writer out of the package.

issues.description: Constants and helpers demoted to package-private create a hidden coupling between format and test-only writer
issues.detail: NAME, QUANTIZED_VECTOR_COMPONENT, rawVectorFormat, calculateDefaultConfidenceInterval all became package-private. The RW test classes now reach into these from the same package. That's an implicit 'these are public to my friends' contract, which is exactly the kind of incidental complexity that grows. Either keep them explicitly public on the format (they describe the on-disk value) or pass them as data into the test writer.

issues.description: PR description acknowledges Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorScorer cannot move yet — partial decomposition left in place
issues.detail: The author explicitly notes the scorer can't be moved. That means after this PR, the 'legacy scalar format' identity is split: most pieces live in backward_codecs.lucene99, but the scorer still lives in core. Readers across the boundary will work, but the conceptual line 'old format = backward_codecs' is now a half-truth. Worth a tracking issue and a comment in the format javadoc naming the remaining dependency.

review.summary: The move itself is the right direction: separating 'codecs we still write' from 'codecs we only read' is a real decomposition along a value/time axis (old on-disk values must still be read; new writes use the new format). What's complected is the read-only-ness: instead of expressing it in the type (no writer method at all on the backward format), the PR keeps fieldsWriter and throws, then quietly re-attaches write capability via test-only RW subclasses that share package-private state. That's easy, not simple. The visibility downgrades (protected to package-private, public to package-private on NAME, rawVectorFormat, helpers) create an implicit 'friends in this package' contract with the test writer that will be load-bearing the next time someone touches this code. The remaining Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorScorer dependency in core means the 'legacy = backward_codecs' identity is partial — fine for this PR, but worth naming explicitly so the next reader isn't surprised.
